title: Amen, once more
hookLine: the first word you learned: let it be so
tomorrow: if you could keep only one commandment, which would it be?

lines: A CROWD, HANDS IN THE AIR.
cards: A friend sends a long, heartfelt message, and the reply that fits is one word. Yes. Same.

Exactly. In the book of Nehemiah, a crowd stands in a city street from morning until midday while the Law is read aloud. Then Ezra blesses God, and "all the people answered, Amen, Amen, with lifting up their hands."
A whole crowd, one word, hands in the air. That word was the first this path gave you.

teach.b: Back then it was simple: amen, let it be so. Five years on, it has company. In the Bible it can be the listener's answer: someone prays, and everyone else signs their name to it.
Paul counts on that when he asks how a listener who can't follow the words could "say Amen at thy giving of thanks". Amen means: I heard that, and I'm in.
Then Paul turns the word toward God's side: "For all the promises of God in him are yea, and in him Amen." Every promise gets a yes.

And in Revelation, Christ is called by the word itself: "These things saith the Amen, the faithful and true witness." So one small word holds three things: the people's answer, God's yes to the promises, and a name.
Under this whole week it was waiting. All things new. Love enters.
The greatest is love. Their words, your road. Our Father.
Every one of those days could close the same way.

how: Christians say amen at the end of prayers, and in some services the congregation answers amen aloud together after a prayer, a blessing or a creed.

o: please, said before asking God for help
let it be so: the listener's yes
the end, as in 'that's all for now'

p: the promises are yea and amen

s: amen is only a way of saying 'the end' to a prayer
in the Bible it's the listener's yes, God's yes to the promises, and a name.
in Revelation, Christ is called 'the Amen'
'These things saith the Amen, the faithful and true witness' (Revelation 3:14).
in Nehemiah, the people answer the reading in silence
'all the people answered, Amen, Amen, with lifting up their hands.'

games.q: you're asked to say grace at a dinner where half the guests don't speak your language. what's Paul's worry in 1 Corinthians?
o: that God won't understand the words.
that you'll sound like you're showing off.
that the listeners can't say amen to what they didn't follow.
games.why: Paul asks how someone who can't follow 'shall say Amen at thy giving of thanks.' amen is the listener's part: they need to hear it to say yes to it.

practice: Count three moments from these five years that you're grateful for: a first word, a story, a hard day that turned. Give each one a few slow breaths of its own. Then, after each, say amen, or simply, let it be so.

wordCard.voice: Amen. The first word on this path, and still the people's answer, God's yes, and a name.

orig.note: Greek, carried over from Hebrew: amen. Revelation 3:14 uses it as a name: the Amen.

carryVoice: Your line: let it be so. Seven days of looking back, and each could end with this one word. Amen to the week.
